title: Frontier AI labs say their models refuted the Exponential Time Hypothesis. What does that mean?
slides: Can a machine refute a mathematical conjecture?
Labs claim their models disproved the Exponential Time Hypothesis.
But the proof only runs three minutes before collapsing.
Check whether any complexity theorist has verified the result.
Ask what a model's confidence actually proves.
thread_text:
1. The 3-minute disproof

A team announced their AI had refuted the Exponential Time Hypothesis — a cornerstone of complexity theory. The proof held up for exactly three minutes before collapsing.

2. Why ETH matters

If ETH falls, hundreds of hardness results fall with it. That's why labs are racing to be the first to say a machine did it.

3. The collapse mechanism

The model produced a chain of reasoning that looked valid until a human checked one step. The error wasn't arithmetic — it was a subtle misreading of a definition.

4. The missing verification

No complexity theorist has confirmed the result. Until one does, the claim is a press release, not a proof.

5. Your turn to check

Next time you see 'AI disproves X', ask: has a domain expert verified it? If not, treat it as a hypothesis, not a fact. Try it on the next headline you read.

An AI reportedly disproved a major math conjecture — and the proof fell apart in three minutes. 🧮
